analysis.note: Correlative adjective, agreeing with arthaḥ; Śaṅkara glosses it as yāvat-parimāṇaḥ. Stem recorded as yāvant for the inflected form yāvān; MW’s lexical headword is yāvat.
The supplied verse prints artha before udapāne; the pausal nominative singular is arthaḥ, also found in the commentary.
Locative singular; Śaṅkara construes it as a limited water-source such as a well or tank.
Analyzed as one compound word; the first member is the past participial stem saṃpluta from sam-√plu. Śaṅkara’s saṃplutodaka-sthānīyam confirms the compound stem.

verification.detail: compound stem saṃplutodaka as Napumsaka/Saptami/Eka: pass; relation karmadharaya: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Correlative adjective, with arthaḥ understood; Śaṅkara glosses it as tāvat-parimāṇa. Stem recorded as tāvant for the inflected form tāvān; MW’s lexical headword is tāvat.
Śaṅkara construes “in all the Vedas” as “in the Veda-enjoined rites.”
Genitive singular; Śaṅkara glosses the referent as a saṃnyāsin.
Present active participle, genitive singular masculine, agreeing with brāhmaṇasya; Śaṅkara supplies its object as paramārtha-tattvam.

justifications.decision: The verse is not read temporally (“as long as ... so long”) but quantitatively, since Śaṅkara glosses both correlatives with parimāṇa, measure/extent.
options_considered: temporal yāvat/tāvat: “as long as ... so long”
justifications.chosen: yāvān ... tāvān expresses correlative measure: “as much ... just so much.”

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara glosses artha in the water example as phala and prayojana, and in the Vedic analogue as karma-phala and vijñāna-phala.
justifications.chosen: artha is translated as “purpose/use/result,” not as semantic “meaning,” wealth, or object.

evidence.translation: the artha such as bathing and drinking is fruit, purpose.
the artha there is the fruit of action.
the artha there is the fruit of knowledge.

justifications.decision: The singular udapāna is not treated narrowly as one particular well; Śaṅkara explicitly expands it to many such limited-water sources.
options_considered: a class of limited water-sources such as wells and tanks
justifications.chosen: udapāne denotes a limited water-source, exemplified by wells and tanks.

evidence.translation: in many water-sources such as wells and tanks, with limited water.

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara says that all the limited purposes of wells and tanks are fulfilled in, and included within, the all-around flooded water. This rules out a commentary-blind rendering in which the point is merely that wells become useless during a flood.
options_considered: a flood making a well useless
a separate adjective+noun split rather than a compound
all-around flooded water that includes the limited purposes
justifications.chosen: sarvataḥ saṃplutodake is “in water flooded on every side,” the inclusive counterpart to the limited well/tank water.

evidence.quote: sa sarvo 'rthaḥ sarvataḥ saṃplutodake 'pi yo 'rthaḥ tāvān eva saṃpadyate, tatra antarbhavatīty arthaḥ
evidence.translation: all that purpose is fulfilled as just that much also in the water flooded on every side; the meaning is that it is included there.
the fruit of knowledge occupies the position of the all-around flooded water.

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara construes the locative not merely as the textual Vedas or sacred lore in general, but as the karmas taught by the Vedas and their fruits.
options_considered: all Vedic texts as textual meaning
the rites enjoined in all the Vedas and their fruits
justifications.chosen: sarveṣu vedeṣu is interpreted as “in all Veda-enjoined rites,” and their artha as karma-phala.

evidence.quote: sarveṣu vedeṣu vedokteṣu karmasu yo 'rthaḥ yat karma-phalaṃ
evidence.translation: the artha in all the Vedas, that is, in the rites taught by the Vedas, is the fruit of action.

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara identifies the brāhmaṇa here with a saṃnyāsin and specifies the object of knowing as paramārtha-tattva, ultimate reality.
options_considered: a caste Brāhmaṇa simply as such
the renouncer who knows ultimate reality
justifications.chosen: brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ means “for/of the Brāhmaṇa, the renouncer, who knows ultimate reality.”

evidence.translation: of the Brāhmaṇa, the renouncer, who knows the truth of ultimate reality.

justifications.decision: Although the knower’s knowledge-fruit includes the fruits of Veda-enjoined rites, Śaṅkara adds that before eligibility for steadfast knowledge, one who is qualified for karma must still perform karma.
options_considered: all ritual action is useless for everyone immediately
ritual action remains obligatory before eligibility for jñāna-niṣṭhā
justifications.chosen: The verse is not a blanket rejection of karma for everyone.

evidence.quote: tasmāt prāk jñāna-niṣṭhādhikāra-prāpteḥ karmaṇy adhikṛtena kūpa-taḍāgādy-artha-sthānīyam api karma kartavyam
evidence.translation: therefore, before attaining eligibility for steadfastness in knowledge, karma—though occupying the place of the purposes of wells, tanks, and the like—must be done by one qualified for karma.

translation:
Whatever purpose/result (artha) there is in a water-source—a well or tank—
[all that] is fulfilled in water flooded on every side;
just that much [fruit], in all the Vedas—that is, in Veda-enjoined rites—
is [included] for the Brāhmaṇa (brāhmaṇa), the renouncer (saṃnyāsin), who knows ultimate reality (paramārtha-tattva).
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render artha as “meaning” and make the verse about the semantic content of the Vedas; Śaṅkara makes it purpose/result, specifically karma-phala and vijñāna-phala.
It might say simply, “a well is useless when there is a flood.” Śaṅkara’s point is inclusion: the purposes of limited water-sources are fulfilled within water flooded on every side.
It might take sarveṣu vedeṣu as the Vedic texts in general. Śaṅkara narrows the comparison to Veda-enjoined rites and their fruits.
It might take brāhmaṇa as a caste label. Śaṅkara glosses the brāhmaṇa here as a saṃnyāsin who knows paramārtha-tattva.
It might infer a universal dismissal of karma; Śaṅkara explicitly preserves the obligation of karma before eligibility for jñāna-niṣṭhā.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 gives yāvān with lemma yāvat. After the verifier report, I record the inflectional stem as yāvant: yāvat Pum/Prathama/Eka derives yāvat/yāvad, not yāvān.

The source text prints artha before udapāne, while ByT5 normalizes arthaḥ. I set the pausal surface to arthaḥ but the surface_in_sandhi to the printed artha; the nominative syntax and Śaṅkara’s arthaḥ support the restoration.
ByT5 segments saṃplutodake as saṃpluta + udake. I analyze the printed form as the single compound stem saṃplutodaka, Napumsaka Saptami Eka, because Śaṅkara cites saṃplutodaka-sthānīyam at line 2.
ByT5 gives tāvān with lemma tāvat. After the verifier report, I record the inflectional stem as tāvant: tāvat Pum/Prathama/Eka derives tāvat/tāvad, not tāvān.

ByT5 gives vijānataḥ under the verbal lemma vijñā. For the required nominal analysis I record the participial stem vijānat, with root jñā and prefix vi; this is a formatting/morphology override, not a semantic disagreement.
mula: yāvān artha udapāne sarvataḥ saṃplutodake | tāvān sarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
commentary_lines: yathā loke kūpa-taḍāgādy-anekasmin udapāne paricchinnodake yāvān yāvat-parimāṇaḥ snāna-pānādir arthaḥ phalaṃ prayojanaṃ sa sarvo 'rthaḥ sarvataḥ saṃplutodake 'pi yo 'rthaḥ tāvān eva saṃpadyate, tatra antarbhavatīty arthaḥ |

evaṃ tāvān tāvat-parimāṇa eva saṃpadyate sarveṣu vedeṣu vedokteṣu karmasu yo 'rthaḥ yat karma-phalaṃ so 'rthaḥ brāhmaṇasya saṃnyāsinaḥ paramārtha-tattvaṃ vijānataḥ yo 'rthaḥ yat vijñāna-phalaṃ sarvataḥ saṃplutodaka-sthānīyaṃ tasmin tāvān eva saṃpadyate tatraivāntarbhavatīty arthaḥ |
yathā kṛtāya vijitāyādhareyāḥ saṃyanty evam enaṃ sarvaṃ tad abhisameti yat kiṃcit prajāḥ sādhu kurvanti yas tad veda yat sa veda [chāu 4.1.2] iti śruteḥ |
tasmāt prāk jñāna-niṣṭhādhikāra-prāpteḥ karmaṇy adhikṛtena kūpa-taḍāgādy-artha-sthānīyam api karma kartavyam ||bhgs_2.46||
